柳琴常見於中國戲曲伴奏，如柳琴戲、泗州戲、亂彈，亦用於常州絲弦。在國樂團中，它屬: The liuqin is common in Chinese opera accompaniment, such as liuqin opera, Sizhou opera and luantan, and also in Changzhou silk-string music. In the Chinese orchestra it is the treble instrument of the plucked section, often playing the melody or florid passagework in the high register, and it can also lead. After the 1970s the liuqin moved from accompaniment to solo playing, and solo pieces and concertos were written for it; when listening, note Wang Huiran's Spring Comes to the Yi River, Liu Xijin's Sketches of Life among the Northern Peoples, and Su Wenqing and Zheng Cuiping's Courtyard after the Rain.
柳琴早期琴身多用柳木，專業用者則以紅檀木或玫瑰木製成；現代版本面板為桐木，背板為: Early liuqin bodies were mostly willow, while professional instruments are made of red sandalwood or rosewood; modern versions have a paulownia soundboard and a red sandalwood back. The strings changed from the early silk to steel. Plectra are commonly celluloid, plastic, horn or tortoiseshell; early players also used a bamboo tube or a hollowed cow horn slipped over the finger to pluck. The materials of the other parts are not stated in the sources.
柳琴是中國的高音撥弦樂器，外形似琵琶而較小、短、圓潤，有梨形共鳴箱，面板開兩個音: The liuqin is a Chinese treble plucked instrument, shaped like a small, short, rounded pipa, with a pear-shaped soundbox, two soundholes in the soundboard, and the strings carried over a bridge; modern instruments commonly have three, four or five strings, and it is held diagonally across the chest and played with a plectrum, with technique close to the mandolin and frequent tremolo. It belongs to the family of Chinese plucked instruments and was formerly used mostly to accompany liuqin opera, Sizhou opera, luantan and Changzhou silk-string music; since the 1970s it has also been used in Chinese orchestra playing and as a solo instrument.
柳琴為高音撥弦樂器，音域高於其他中國撥弦樂器，音色洪亮清脆，具穿透力，常在高音區: The liuqin is a treble plucked instrument, higher in range than other Chinese plucked instruments, with a loud, clear, penetrating tone, often playing the melody or florid passages in the high register. The sound begins when the plectrum touches the string, and force and colour are controlled with tremolo, repeated strokes and harmonics; a strong stroke is tense and excited, a soft one quiet and sweet. Its frets are high, so the fingers do not touch the body, which helps tone and intonation but makes chords harder. It is smaller than the pipa and is held and plucked like the zhongruan and the yueqin, so players of those instruments often double on it.
柳琴自唐代普通琵琶演化而来，早期流行于山东，宋代传入江苏，明代流入安徽。清代因音: The liuqin evolved from the ordinary pipa of the Tang dynasty, was popular in Shandong early on, passed to Jiangsu in the Song and reached Anhui in the Ming. In the Qing, because its tone was clear and strong, it spread nationwide with the fashion for opera and became the accompanying instrument of liuqin opera, Sizhou opera, luantan and Changzhou silk-string music; the name and the definition of "liuqin" were only settled in the late Qing. In 1958 Wang Huiran set a unified definition, dividing the instrument into three-string and four-string treble liuqin, with the frets increased to 24 and 29 and a plectrum adopted. In the 1970s the four-string treble liuqin appeared, using bamboo in place of sorghum stalk and steel wire in place of silk strings, which widened its range and its expression. From the 1980s it entered the Chinese orchestra as a treble plucked instrument and developed as a solo instrument.

演奏柳琴時端坐，將琴斜置胸前，左手拇指輕扶琴頸，以可自如上下換把為準則，四指獨立: To play the liuqin, sit upright and hold the instrument diagonally against the chest; the left thumb rests lightly on the neck, just enough to shift positions freely, and the four fingers stop the strings independently; the right hand is half closed, the thumb and index finger pinching the plectrum, and the thumb must not sink in when the plectrum touches the string. A beginner can first practise the down stroke, the up stroke, the double down stroke, the double up stroke and the tremolo, then add vibrato, hammered notes, pulled notes, pushed and pulled strings, and harmonics.
